functions.name: oceanbase::common::murmurhash64A
functions.signature: inline uint64_t oceanbase::common::murmurhash64A(const void *key, int32_t len, uint64_t seed)
functions.description: Computes a 64-bit MurmurHash2 (64A variant) of the input buffer using the provided seed. Intended for fast, non-cryptographic hashing on 64-bit platforms. Usage: pass a pointer to a byte buffer, its length in bytes, and a 64-bit seed to obtain a 64-bit hash value. Caveats: not endian-neutral and may have alignment considerations across platforms.
requirements: If len > 0, key must point to a readable buffer of at least len bytes.
On platforms that require aligned memory access, key should be 8-byte aligned to avoid faults because the implementation reads uint64_t values directly.
Hash is non-cryptographic and not suitable for security-sensitive purposes.
Behavior and results are platform/endian dependent; do not compare hash values across differing endianness platforms.

functions.name: oceanbase::common::murmurhash2
functions.signature: uint32_t oceanbase::common::murmurhash2(const void *data, int32_t len, uint32_t hash)
functions.description: Computes a 32-bit MurmurHash2 of the input buffer with the given initial hash (seed). Faster and better mixed than some older hashes; not endian-neutral. Only declared in this header; implementation is external.
requirements: If len > 0, data must point to a readable buffer of at least len bytes.
Hash is non-cryptographic; do not use for security-sensitive contexts.
Results may vary across platforms due to endianness; avoid cross-platform comparisons.

functions.name: oceanbase::common::murmurhash
functions.signature: inline uint64_t oceanbase::common::murmurhash(const void *data, int32_t len, uint64_t hash)
functions.description: Public wrapper that computes a 64-bit MurmurHash (MurmurHash2 64A variant) of the input buffer using the provided seed. Preferred entry point per comment.
requirements: If len > 0, data must point to a readable buffer of at least len bytes.
On platforms that require aligned memory access, data should be 8-byte aligned to avoid faults (internally reads uint64_t).
Non-cryptographic; not suitable for security-sensitive uses.
Hash values are endian/platform dependent.

functions.name: oceanbase::common::appname_hash
functions.signature: inline uint64_t oceanbase::common::appname_hash(const void *data, int32_t len, uint64_t hash)
functions.description: Alias/wrapper for the 64-bit MurmurHash2 (64A variant). Intended to hash application names or similar identifiers with a given seed; returns a 64-bit hash of the buffer.
requirements: If len > 0, data must point to a readable buffer of at least len bytes.
On platforms that require aligned memory access, data should be 8-byte aligned to avoid faults (internally reads uint64_t).
Non-cryptographic; not suitable for security-sensitive uses.
Hash values are endian/platform dependent.

functions.name: oceanbase::common::fnv_hash2
functions.signature: uint32_t oceanbase::common::fnv_hash2(const void *data, int32_t len, uint32_t hash)
functions.description: Computes a 32-bit FNV-style hash of the input buffer with the given initial hash (seed). Only declared here; implementation is external. Exact variant (FNV-1 vs FNV-1a) is unspecified in this header.
requirements: If len > 0, data must point to a readable buffer of at least len bytes.
Non-cryptographic; not suitable for security-sensitive uses.
Without the implementation, exact seed semantics and cross-platform determinism are unknown.

functions.name: oceanbase::common::rotl32
functions.signature: inline uint32_t oceanbase::common::rotl32(uint32_t x, int8_t r)
functions.description: Performs a 32-bit left rotate of x by r bits. Utility used by MurmurHash3 routines.
requirements: r must be in the range 0 <= r < 32; shifting by 32 or more is undefined behavior in C/C++.
No special alignment or state requirements.

functions.name: oceanbase::common::getblock32
functions.signature: inline uint32_t oceanbase::common::getblock32(const uint32_t *p, int i)
functions.description: Returns the 32-bit word at p[i]. Used by MurmurHash3 to fetch 32-bit blocks, including with negative indices when p points past the logical start of the block array.
requirements: p must be a valid pointer such that the element at index i is readable; i may be negative if and only if p is positioned so that p+i refers to a valid element.
Dereferencing an invalid index leads to undefined behavior; callers must ensure bounds/positioning.

functions.name: oceanbase::common::fmix32
functions.description: Finalization mix function for 32-bit hash values (from MurmurHash3). It avalanches all bits of h to finalize the hash.
requirements: No preconditions beyond providing any 32-bit input value.
Deterministic across platforms supporting 32-bit unsigned arithmetic.

functions.name: oceanbase::common::murmurhash3_x86_32
functions.signature: inline uint32_t oceanbase::common::murmurhash3_x86_32(const void *key, int32_t len, uint32_t seed)
functions.description: Computes the 32-bit MurmurHash3 (x86_32) of the input buffer with the given seed. Used here to calculate bucket partitions (e.g., for iceberg tables). Processes 4-byte blocks and tails, then applies fmix32 for finalization.
requirements: If len > 0, key must point to a readable buffer of at least len bytes.
Endianness and alignment follow MurmurHash3 x86 reference behavior; avoid cross-endian comparisons of hash outputs.
Non-cryptographic; not suitable for security-sensitive uses.

Consumers read exactly len bytes from the start of the buffer; contents are treated as opaque data for hashing or similar byte-wise processing.

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator targets arbitrary binary data consumers (hash functions).
# The fuzz stubs copy a std::string into an internal aligned buffer and choose len in [0, 1024].
# We therefore generate a bytes payload (<= 1024, but we will allow up to 2048 since FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# can be longer; the stub will cap len to <= size and <= 1024). We focus on producing diverse,
# valid, and interesting binary patterns that exercise different block/tail paths and alignment-like
# behaviors in the hashers.

MAX_OUT = 4096  # overall cap per instructions
MAX_STR = 2048  # provide ample data; stub caps len to 1024

# Precompute some pattern chunks commonly interesting for hash routines
_DEF_SEEDS_64 = [
    0, 1, 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF, 0x0123456789ABCDEF,
    0x5555555555555555, 0xAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA, 0xDEADBEEFCAFEBABE,
]
_DEF_SEEDS_32 = [0, 1, 0xFFFFFFFF, 0x9747b28c, 0x85ebca6b, 0xc2b2ae35]

# Useful byte patterns
PAT_ZERO = bytes()
PAT_ALL_ZERO = b"\x00" * 1024
PAT_ALL_FF = b"\xFF" * 1024
PAT_ASCII = (
    b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ"
    b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
    b"0123456789_-.:/\\@#\n\r\t"
)
PAT_UTF8_LIKE = (
    # mixture of ASCII and multi-byte sequences (valid & invalid) as opaque bytes
    b"hello-\xe2\x98\x83-\xf0\x9f\x92\xa9-\xed\xa0\x80-\xc3\x28"
)
PAT_INC = bytes([i & 0xFF for i in range(256)])
PAT_DEC = bytes([(-i) & 0xFF for i in range(256)])

# Block-aligned patterns for 4 and 8 bytes boundaries
BLOCK8 = b"ABCDEFGH" * 64  # 512 bytes
BLOCK4 = b"WXYZ" * 128     # 512 bytes

# Tail-sensitive sizes for Murmur: lengths mod 4 (for x86_32) and mod 8 (64A)
TAIL_SIZES = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]


def _rand_int(rng: random.Random, a: int, b: int) -> int:
    return rng.randint(a, b)


def _choose(rng: random.Random, seq: List):
    return seq[rng.randrange(len(seq))]


def _gen_len_for_hash_paths(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Prefer lengths up to 1024 to match stub cap; pick with bias to interesting tails
    # 60%: tailored lengths to hit specific tail remainders; 40%: arbitrary
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        base = _rand_int(rng, 0, 1024)
        # Snap to interesting remainders with some probability
        if rng.random() < 0.7:
            # choose whether to bias for 4- or 8-byte tail
            if rng.random() < 0.5:
                # enforce len % 4 in {0,1,2,3}
                rem = _choose(rng, [0, 1, 2, 3])
                base = base - (base % 4) + rem
            else:
                rem = _choose(rng, [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7])
                base = base - (base % 8) + rem
        # clamp
        return max(0, min(1024, base))
    else:
        return _rand_int(rng, 0, 1024)


def _mix_chunks(chunks: List[bytes], target_len: int, rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    while len(out) < target_len and chunks:
        ch = _choose(rng, chunks)
        # Optionally slice chunk to random piece
        if len(ch) > 0 and rng.random() < 0.6:
            start = _rand_int(rng, 0, max(0, len(ch) - 1)) if len(ch) > 1 else 0
            end = _rand_int(rng, start, len(ch))
            part = ch[start:end]
        else:
            part = ch
        need = target_len - len(out)
        if len(part) > need:
            part = part[:need]
        out += part
    # If still short, pad with small random data
    if len(out) < target_len:
        pad_len = target_len - len(out)
        out += bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(pad_len))
    return bytes(out)


def _embed_seeds(buf: bytearray, rng: random.Random):
    # Occasionally prefix or suffix with seed bytes to mimic realistic inputs that sometimes
    # include numeric identifiers at start/end.
    action = rng.random()
    if action < 0.33 and len(buf) <= 1016:  # room for 8 bytes prefix
        seed = _choose(rng, _DEF_SEEDS_64)
        prefix = struct.pack('<Q', seed) if rng.random() < 0.5 else struct.pack('>Q', seed)
        buf[:0] = prefix
    elif action < 0.66 and len(buf) <= 1016:
        seed = _choose(rng, _DEF_SEEDS_64)
        suffix = struct.pack('<Q', seed) if rng.random() < 0.5 else struct.pack('>Q', seed)
        buf += suffix
    else:
        # maybe 32-bit seed in the middle
        if len(buf) >= 8:
            pos = _rand_int(rng, 0, len(buf) - 4)
            seed32 = _choose(rng, _DEF_SEEDS_32)
            val = struct.pack('<I', seed32) if rng.random() < 0.5 else struct.pack('>I', seed32)
            buf[pos:pos+4] = val


def _build_payload(rng: random.Random, target_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Assemble from diverse chunks to stress different code paths
    chunks = [
        PAT_ASCII,
        PAT_UTF8_LIKE,
        PAT_INC,
        PAT_DEC,
        BLOCK8,
        BLOCK4,
        b"\x00\x01\x02\x03\x04\x05\x06\x07",
        b"\xFF\xFE\xFD\xFC\xFB\xFA\xF9\xF8",
    ]
    # Occasionally use uniform buffers
    pick = rng.random()
    if pick < 0.1:
        base = PAT_ALL_ZERO
    elif pick < 0.2:
        base = PAT_ALL_FF
    else:
        base = _mix_chunks(chunks, target_len, rng)
    if len(base) < target_len:
        base = base + bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(target_len - len(base)))
    elif len(base) > target_len:
        base = base[:target_len]
    buf = bytearray(base)

    # Optionally embed seed-like numbers to vary early/late bytes
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        _embed_seeds(buf, rng)
        # Ensure we still respect the 1024 cap used by stubs
        if len(buf) > 1024:
            del buf[1024:]
    return bytes(buf)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose target length leaning toward the stub cap and interesting tails
    length = _gen_len_for_hash_paths(rng)

    # Small probability to generate empty input
    if rng.random() < 0.05:
        length = 0

    # Build payload
    payload = _build_payload(rng, length)

    # Final clamp to constraints
    if len(payload) > MAX_STR:
        payload = payload[:MAX_STR]
    if len(payload) > MAX_OUT:
        payload = payload[:MAX_OUT]

    return payload
